how: Capoeira Club London (founded 2012 by Mestre Hiram Ribeiro) runs around 40 classes a week across the city, alongside Cordao de Ouro and Grupo Muzenza.
Traditional Bela Deri silat meets weekly at SOAS and sport-focused pencak silat runs in Walthamstow, open to beginners.
Kew Gardens has a Treetop Walkway about 200 m long, roughly 18 m above ground in a woodland canopy.
Raging Dragons trains on Sunday mornings at the Docklands Sailing and Watersports Centre and invites newcomers to try dragon boating.
Wakeup Docklands runs a 2-point cable wakeboarding system in the Royal Docks with beginner (Blue) 15-minute sessions.
Cable towing in London is wakeboard-oriented at Wakeup Docklands; no dedicated cable water-ski operation was confirmed.
Wakeup Docklands offers a one-hour Introduction to Paddleboarding for complete beginners plus a BSUPA Ready2Ride course and private SUP hire.
The Long Walk Chinese Orchestra accepts beginners and experienced players, with music leaders teaching ruan, liuqin, erhu, pipa and dizi.
The UK Chinese Music Ensemble and London Youlan Qin Society offer erhu classes at beginner and intermediate levels, plus a summer school at SOAS.
The UK Chinese Music Ensemble and London Youlan Qin Society offer guzheng classes at beginner and intermediate levels, plus a summer school at SOAS.
London Dance Academy runs beginner aerial silks courses in five-week blocks, and Aerial Gymnastics London teaches adult silks and hoop in Beckton.
Studios such as Akila Pole Studio and The Factory London and university clubs run beginner pole classes.
Wakeup Docklands offers paddleboarding in the Royal Docks and its site shows yoga on a deck, but SUP yoga is not listed as a bookable session.
